title: Fix memory rejection boundaries and clarify Server/KB ownership
body:
The Atlas review exposed a mismatch between the configured PostgreSQL runtime role and rejection-record protections, plus different canonicalization in the Go owner and database guard. This PR closes those gaps and updates the documentation against testing baseline 6cd136947.

- Revoke refusal DELETE/TRUNCATE privileges during schema replay and current role provisioning; add an actual-login CI regression for aimee_store_runtime.
- Remove legacy PostgreSQL adoption: no old administrator fallback, aimee_shared rename, application ownership sweep, or blanket grants on existing objects. Retain fresh provisioning and current-role credential refresh before opening TCP. Replace legacy-upgrade tests with current bootstrap/restart coverage.
- Backfill an indexed, generated rejection identity using PostgreSQL 18 Unicode normalization and full folding. Both the Go lookup and direct-writer guard use it, including edge-class transitions.
- Reject direct model-authored instruction overrides before memory writes and fact endpoint registration, with explicit refusal receipts. This bounded check preserves quoted examples and verified user text; serving-time integrity checks remain mandatory.
- Expose correction proposals in Memory Center with explicit store selection, source/draft comparison, exact version/digest, conflict handling, and reviewer attribution. Present due decisions as an actionable operator queue.
- Correlate shared-memory evidence events with durable audit intents and document pending delivery versus verified chain evidence.
- Add a canonical Server/KB boundary guide and update architecture, deployment, storage, retrieval, API, and operational documentation.

Validation: Go memory unit suite; full PostgreSQL runtime-role replay; fact, public-store, personal/shared correction, actual-login privilege and audit-correlation tests; existing-row schema upgrade and two replays; 9 frontend tests; TypeScript and both production builds. Clean-checkout schema parity, memory ownership, generated-doc, and full documentation checks pass.

After removing legacy adoption, local PostgreSQL 18 checks also passed for fresh provisioning, repeated provisioning, owner/ACL preservation, runtime writes, password rotation, and retired-admin rejection. Shell syntax and test registration checks pass. The replacement Docker restart/TLS test is wired into CI; Docker is unavailable locally.

Existing volumes must already use the current database/role layout. The generated refusal column backfills under a table lock during schema migration. No production migration or deployment was performed. UI tests use mocked transport; no deployed authentication end-to-end claim. Unrelated research drafts and benchmark artifacts are excluded.
head: fix/atlas-memory-boundaries
